title: Writing down the Missourians' head arrangements; Cozy Cole's dance-school band
summary: Finding the band plays only head arrangements, Thomas starts writing parts and sells his first arrangements to Cozy Cole; he also recalls Omar Simeon from Jelly's band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And when Scotty... Poor Scotty. When Scotty got out of jail, he didn't have no job. Because man, I got in there and I... And when I first got in there, them guys were playing all head arrangements; I said, "You'all got to be crazy. You got to write some of this stuff down. Because whoever comes in the band and has to play in somebody's place has got to have something to play." And I started to do a little writing, because I had just started to write. And Cozy Cole was one of the first bands I started arranging for...

Yeah, Cozy had a little band. He was playing in one of them dance schools. See, in them early days with them dance schools, if you got a dance school job, you had a job. So I sold my little arrangements to...
So he had a band, right?

Yes. I think it was "Let Me Call You Sweetheart." That's how I first met Cozy. I went and rehearsed his band. I'd seen Jelly Roll rehearse, and I picked up on that, and I rehearsed. If I heard the arrangement today, I know it would be sad. But it was the best I could write then.
Another thing I wanted to tell you about Jelly. I knew Simeon, because Simeon...
Yeah, Omar Simeon. He used to play with Jelly. Thing is...
Where did you know Simeon from?
I think I knew him from Milwaukee.
But he'd come from New Orleans...
But he was from New Orleans. He was from New Orleans, yeah. And I liked all them guys, because I know what they played...
